---
title: "M: Musculo-skeletal system"
description: "ATC group M for modellers: four unrelated PD paradigms under one letter, with notes held at M01, M03, M04 and M05."
date: "2026-02-08"
---

Drugs for joint, bone and muscle disease, plus the neuromuscular blockers given under anaesthesia [@sheinerSimultaneousModelingPharmacokinetics1979].
Published models here span a subjective pain score [@mandemaPopulationPharmacodynamicModel1996] and an evoked muscle twitch [@sheinerSimultaneousModelingPharmacokinetics1979].

In 1938 Richard Gill returned from the Amazon with 11 kg of curare, from which Squibb isolated a standardised extract; Harold Griffith and Enid Johnson gave it in the operating room in 1942 [@elsherbiniConnectionHaroldGriffith2024; @griffithUseCurareGeneral1942].

| Level 2 code | Description | In plain terms | Current standard |
| ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [M01](m01_antiinflammatory-and-antirheumatic-products/) | Antiinflammatory and antirheumatic products |  | Ibuprofen (M01AE01) / naproxen (M01AE02) |
| M02 | Topical products for joint and muscular pain |  | Topical diclofenac (M02AA15) / topical ketoprofen (M02AA10) |
| [M03](m03_muscle-relaxants/) | Muscle relaxants |  | Rocuronium bromide (M03AC09) for neuromuscular block / baclofen (M03BX01) for spasticity |
| [M04](m04_antigout-preparations/) | Antigout preparations |  | Allopurinol (M04AA01) / febuxostat (M04AA03) |
| [M05](m05_drugs-for-treatment-of-bone-diseases/) | Drugs for treatment of bone diseases |  | Alendronic acid (M05BA04) / denosumab (M05BX04) |
| M09 | Other drugs for disorders of the musculo-skeletal system | leftover bone, joint and muscle drugs | Residual catch-all group, but it now carries real drug-level standards for rare neuromuscular disease: nusinersen (M09AX07) and risdiplam (M09AX10) for spinal muscular atrophy |

## Modelling notes

**Endpoint.**
Each level 2 code brings its own: WOMAC pain in M01 [@wenPlaceboResponseOral2022], serum urate in M04 [@murakiPopulationPharmacodynamicAnalysis2018], bone markers and density in M05 [@wuQuantitativePredictionBone2021], evoked twitch in M03 [@jiReversalRocuroniumInducedIntense2023].

**Easy to overlook.**
For M02 the relevant exposure is local, in skin and synovial fluid, and dermal PBPK is what links measured plasma concentration to that site, so [bioequivalence](/docs/concepts/clinpharm-studies/ba-be/) is argued at the site of action alongside, not instead of, a plasma study [@tsakalozouPhysiologicallyBasedPharmacokinetic2021].

**Mechanistic extrapolation.**
A multiscale model of calcium homeostasis and bone remodelling [@petersonPhysiologicallyBasedMathematical2010] was extended to predict lumbar spine density under denosumab, including the decline after discontinuation [@petersonPredictingNonlinearChanges2012].
For M02, dermal PBPK replaced a comparative clinical endpoint study in an FDA generic approval of topical diclofenac gel [@tsakalozouPhysiologicallyBasedPharmacokinetic2021].
